subject: Enclave runbook ownership + ops inventory needed for Greenbank on‑prem feasibility
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enclave runbook ownership + ops inventory needed for Greenbank on‑prem feasibility

Team —

Greenbank wants a concrete feasibility note from us for their on‑prem pilot. I took the call last week; they sent a short requirements doc (attached). Before we create the customer‑facing feasibility brief, I need a compact internal one‑pager covering:

- Technical gaps: what infra/config we don’t yet support for an air‑gapped enclave (HSM/KMS integration, specific L2 networking, approved OS images).
- Operational pre‑reqs: runbook items (day 0 install, key rotation, backups, incident response responsibilities).
- Staffing: who owns day‑0 install, who is oncall post‑launch, and rough t-shirt estimates (SWE/Infra/SRE/Support).
- Timeline risk: blockers and a conservative ETA for an initial pilot.

Action items I’m asking from you now: 
- Karthik: inventory of architecture gaps + a one‑paragraph mitigation approach for each gap.
- Stephanie: draft minimal runbook/rollout roles (attach runbook‑draft.md), and staffing t‑shirt estimates.
- Rishi: quick note on what evidence we’ll need for their SOC‑style checklist (audit trails, retention, HSM).
- Jordan: please paste any notes from customer (they gave a short list in email) and confirm Greenbank contacts.

Please reply with bullets by EOD Wed (2028‑03‑07) so I can fold into the external memo Thursday morning. I attached the Greenbank reqs and a small inventory template — populate enclave_inventory.csv where helpful.

Thanks,

— Olga
Olga Petrov | Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: greenbank_requirements.pdf (pdf), enclave_inventory.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave runbook ownership + ops inventory needed for Greenbank on‑prem feasibility

Olga —

Quick initial pass below (will flesh out into the spreadsheet):

1) HSM/KMS
- Gap: We have KMS integrations for cloud KMSs; no certified on‑prem HSM connector in prod.
- Mitigation: Use customer‑managed HSM gateway (PKCS#11) + a short shim we run as part of the enclave; needs security signoff.

2) Network isolation (L2 requirements)
- Gap: Our current deploy expects routable L3 with specific NAT/BGP rules; Greenbank requires strict L2 isolation for PD.
- Mitigation: Offer a co‑located gateway appliance pattern — place a lightweight packet relay in customer DMZ. Adds ~2 days infra work.

3) Kernel/OS images & GPU drivers
- Gap: We rely on containerized GPU stacks on Ubuntu 22; customer mandates RHEL 8 with specific certified drivers.
- Mitigation: Build RHEL‑based image and validate driver matrix; estimate 1 week QA per GPU family.

4) Audit logs & retention
- Gap: Need to ensure our runtime emits immutable audit logs to a customer endpoint with configurable retention.
- Mitigation: Add log shippers to write to their on‑prem SIEM; small runtime change (3–4 dev days).

I'll add brief cost/time t‑shirts to the inventory CSV. For the pilot, I recommend we avoid building a full HSM adapter — instead accept their PKCS#11 gateway and validate with a joint test.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Staff Architect, Serving Runtime
Attachments: (will update enclave_inventory.csv)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave runbook ownership + ops inventory needed for Greenbank on‑prem feasibility

Adding ops perspective and a first cut runbook (attached). TL;DR: we can support a pilot but need a 2‑phase owner model: Redwood install + handoff to Greenbank ops.

Runbook highlights (see runbook‑draft.md):
- Day 0: deployment checklist (hardware verification, driver matrix, network ports, initial key injection). Owner: Redwood Infra (on‑site/remote during install).
- Day 1‑7: monitoring validation window. Owner: Redwood SRE (rotate into on‑call schedule for 2 weeks).
- Day 14+: Handover docs & runbooks delivered to Greenbank; Support to handle tier‑1 for 30 days, then transition.

Staffing (rough t‑shirts for pilot, 6–8 weeks):
- SWEs (runtime, infra): 2 FTE (0.5 ramped)
- SRE/Infra: 1 full‑time for first 3 weeks, then 0.5 ongoing for 4 weeks
- Solutions/Field eng (install + customer coordination): 1 on‑site day per install + 0.5 remote

Oncall: recommend we assign a dedicated rotation contact (SRE) for first 30 days, then fall back to normal oncall with SLA extension agreed in contract.

I attached the runbook draft and a lightly populated enclave_inventory.csv. Need Karthik to confirm driver and network items. Rishi — please flag any additional evidence items for the runbook (audit, key custody).

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Senior SRE Manager, Redwood Console Team
Attachments: runbook-draft.md (markdown), enclave_inventory.csv (csv)

Subject: Greenbank enclave high‑level requirements
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the call. High level requirements:
1) Data residency: all tokens and ephemeral traces must not leave our network.
2) HSM: we use an HSM cluster exposing PKCS#11; any key operations must go through it.
3) Audit: full immutable trace of token consumption with 13 month retention and export to our Splunk instance.
4) Maintenance window tolerances: max 2 hours scheduled downtime per month.

We are ok with a pilot that uses our gateway shim as Karthik mentioned but need explicit runbook steps and smoke tests. Can you share the runbook draft and a short list of owners for the pilot?

Regards,
Elena Soto
CTO, Greenbank
Greenbank Inc.

---------- End forwarded message ---------

Elena also pinged the IT team (it@greenbank.com) and Rackline (their infra integrator). Jordan here — they want the runbook + owners list (same ask).

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Enclave runbook ownership + ops inventory needed for Greenbank on‑prem feasibility

Thanks all — good progress. Below is the consolidated internal decision we can include in the external feasibility memo: 

1) Architecture gaps & mitigations (summary)\- HSM: accept PKCS#11 gateway for pilot; build HSM adapter only if pilot fails. Owner: Karthik (architecture validation + test).
- Network L2 requirement: proposal = gateway appliance pattern. Owner: Karthik + Stephanie (validation and smoke tests).
- OS/driver matrix: build RHEL images; Owner: Karthik and Infra.
- Audit logging: ship to customer SIEM via logshippers. Owner: Rishi + SRE.

2) Runbook & staffing\- Use Stephanie's runbook‑draft.md as base; Redwood will own Day‑0 install and 14‑day monitoring window. Oncall contact for pilot: Stephanie will nominate SRE rotation. Staffing estimate: SWE 2, SRE 1 (intense first 3 weeks), Solutions 0.5 FTE.

3) Timeline & risk\- Conservative ETA to pilot readiness: 6–8 weeks from approval (driver builds and HSM verification are the biggest risk).

4) Customer asks to include in external memo\- HSM PKCS#11 path, audit retention (13 months), maintenance window limits. Jordan — please confirm contact details and ask Elena for preferred test vectors for smoke tests.

Deliverable: I will draft the external feasibility memo Thursday morning. Karthik — please update enclave_inventory.csv with the RHEL/driver rows and a short t‑shirt for each item by EOD Wed. Stephanie — finalize runbook owners and nominate the oncall contact. Rishi — list the exact evidence items we will attach to their SOC checklist.

If nothing else, I’ll send the customer memo Thursday 10:00 PT and loop in Legal for an entry‑level pilot addendum.

— Olga
Olga Petrov | Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
